I'd skip ahead at 1:01:00 (the narration at 1:01 is 00:01:02,940, so about 1:03), where the video lists what each twin pays: down payment, closing costs, mortgage, tax, insurance, repairs and selling costs. It's a long run of numbers over a mostly static picture of two buildings. I'd also skip the stretch from about 2:00 to 3:03, where the video explains why other rent-or-buy math falls short and then explains the rent tag. That part repeats points the video makes again later, at 8:04 and 8:35. The last section, 9:39 to 10:19, mostly recaps the findings, so I'd skip that too.

2. I was most engaged at 3:44, when the street of houses lights up and the dark doors begin to appear in 2001. The 72-starts, 6-wins result (4:22) and the April 2012 and June 2006 houses (5:13 to 6:00) pay off the opening hook. Seeing the dark block in the middle of the grid, then the darkest house with its two stacks, made the question feel real.
